clue.text: Joan's mate heard of at Epsom

indicators.note: heard tells us the race's name is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: the Derby is the famous horse race run at Epsom

explanation.surface: A question about where Joan's husband was last heard of: at the Epsom races.
explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are the proverbial devoted elderly couple. The Derby, a classic horse race held at Epsom Downs in Surrey, is pronounced 'Darby' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old ballad and the British phrase 'Darby and Joan', he is the faithful husband of Joan.

clue.text: Kitty among the pigs? It's mad

indicators.note: among says one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: a sty is where pigs are kept, so the pigs suggest their sty
kitty is a pet word for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat wandering into a pigsty seems a crazy thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' could suggest a pool of money, but here it is the pet cat put inside the pigs' STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, a mild sense of crazy.

clue.text: Seeming like a subdued mum or dad

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet, subdued playing
either mum or dad is a parent

explanation.surface: Something seems to resemble a meek, quietened mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeming' is the definition at the front; 'like' is only a link word. 'Subdued' gives P, the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means outwardly so, as in 'his apparent calm', which matches seeming.

clue.text: To overpraise is more on the level

definitions.meaning: to praise someone excessively or insincerely
comparative of an adjective meaning even or horizontal

explanation.surface: Praising too much is said to be more honest and level.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere praise is one sense, and the comparative of 'flat' (level, even) is the other.

clue.text: It's futile to go barefoot

definitions.meaning: pointless, achieving nothing
without anything on the feet, read literally as lacking footwear

explanation.surface: Someone claims there is no point in going without shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for unavailing or useless, and read literally, lacking boots, so shoeless.

clue.text: Nell's kinsfolk in Northern Ireland?

parts.note: Nell Gwyn sold oranges, so her fellow traders are men of oranges; in Northern Ireland the same name is borne by members of the Protestant Orange Order

explanation.surface: A query about the relatives of a woman called Nell living in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn, mistress of Charles II, began as an orange-seller in a London theatre; the Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal society in Northern Ireland whose members carry this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order, the Protestant society in Ulster, take their name from William of Orange.

clue.text: His travels were booked to spoil curtailed company horseplay

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
company cut short becomes its standard abbreviation, the first two letters
polo is a game played on horseback, so play on horses

explanation.surface: A man's journeys were reserved in order to ruin a firm's rough fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means written up in a book, not reserved: the Venetian traveller's journeys were recorded in a famous book. 'Horseplay' is read literally as a sport on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant's journeys to China were set down in a celebrated travel book.

clue.text: Try to win favour where justice is administered (3) 10it's not concrete to take away

definitions.meaning: to seek someone's favour or affection, to woo
a law ... where cases are heard

explanation.surface: Seeking favour in the very place where justice is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo or curry favour is one sense; the hall of a judge and jury is the other.

clue.text: No more than a pond

definitions.meaning: only, nothing beyond
a small lake or pool

explanation.surface: A body of water described as nothing more than a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means only or simply; as a noun it is a small lake.

clue.text: It's not concrete to take away

definitions.meaning: existing only as an idea, theoretical
to remove or extract

explanation.surface: Something intangible that is meant to be carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means theoretical; as a verb it means to remove or summarise.

clue.text: Former camper's home range

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: A one-time camper's house and the area around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Range and scope both mean how far something reaches.

clue.text: Apollo's plaything sounds more fitted to Ananias

indicators.note: the instrument's name sounds like a word that suits the clue's biblical character better

parts.note: Ananias in Acts was struck dead for lying, so his name stands for a liar

explanation.surface: Apollo's toy instrument seems more suited to a famous deceiver.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollo, Greek god of music, is shown with a lyre. Ananias was struck dead for lying to the apostles (Acts 5), so his name means a liar, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek god of music, always pictured playing his stringed instrument.

clue.text: Chapel named by Scrooge's parents

definitions.meaning: a common biblical name for a Nonconformist chapel, from 'stone of help' in 1 Samuel
the first name Dickens gave Scrooge in A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A place of worship whose name was chosen by a miser's mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Welsh and English Methodist and Baptist chapels bear this biblical name, which is also Scrooge's given name in Dickens.

clue.text: Mickey's home in Cornwall

definitions.meaning: Mickey Mouse would live in a hole in the skirting
a fishing village near Penzance, in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Mickey lives in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip; the village there is pronounced 'Mowzel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in the wainscot where a cartoon rodent lives, and a Cornish fishing village of the same name.

clue.text: The best policy in the floral border

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that truthfulness is the best policy
a garden flower, Lunaria, with silvery seed pods

explanation.surface: Being truthful is said to be wise, even among the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb praises truthfulness; the garden plant Lunaria shares the name.

clue.text: Mince pie has a healing a effect on gourmets

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the word pie is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: something with a healing effect cures

explanation.surface: Eating a Christmas mince pie does food-lovers a power of good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' looks like the Christmas pastry, but 'Mince' is the anagram signal working on PIE to give EPI; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicures are people devoted to fine food and drink, connoisseurs of the table.

clue.text: Salad stuff and French oil vessel held high

parts.note: cress is a salad leaf
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A list of salad items, a French dressing ingredient and a raised container of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is a metal basket or cup of burning oil mounted on a pole as a beacon.

clue.text: Stop to relax with a shower perhaps

parts.note: to rest is to relax
a shower is one kind of rain

explanation.surface: Someone advised to halt and unwind with a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shower' suggests washing, but it is a brief fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or check someone, preventing them acting.

clue.text: Pseudonym for Mrs Swan, the writer

definitions.text: Pseudonym for Mrs Swan, the writer

parts.words: Pseudonym for Mrs Swan, the writer
parts.note: a female swan is called a pen; a writer's pseudonym has the same name

explanation.surface: An author named Mrs Swan adopts an alias.
explanation.walkthrough: A female swan is a pen and the male a cob, so 'Mrs Swan' is literally a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's assumed name, used instead of the real one on published work.

clue.text: Thus Captain Hook appears to the sound of heavy breathing

parts.note: as can mean thus, in the manner of
Captain Hook in Peter Pan is a pirate

explanation.surface: The villain of Peter Pan arrives accompanied by loud panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appears to' is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a breathed sound, like the h at the start of 'hat', made with a puff of air.

clue.text: A bit of legal sorcery as well

indicators.note: a bit of says the letters are a small part taken from inside the phrase legal sorcery

explanation.surface: Lawyers' trickery is partly magic too.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and as well both mean in addition, besides.

clue.text: Wine to plunder

definitions.meaning: an old fortified white wine from Spain, as drunk by Falstaff
to pillage or loot a town

explanation.surface: Raiding the cellar for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry-like Spanish wine of Shakespeare's day, and to loot a captured place.

clue.text: Interrupts to reduce moral transgression

parts.note: to cut is to reduce
a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: Breaking in to cut down on wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts in breaks into another's conversation or line.

clue.text: Trade mark for a hot iron

definitions.meaning: a maker's name or label on goods
a heated iron used to mark cattle or burn a sign

explanation.surface: A heated metal tool used to stamp a company's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A product's label or name, and the heated iron for burning a mark on livestock.

clue.text: Shot us indiscriminately, resulting in loud cries

indicators.note: indiscriminately means without order, so the letters of shot us are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone fired at us at random, provoking yells.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts and loud cries are both yells.

clue.text: Misdirected Turner on one-way trip

indicators.note: misdirected means sent the wrong way, so the letters of Turner on are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turner was sent off the wrong way on a journey he can't come back from.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way trip is a journey with no coming back.

clue.text: A right of possession for extra-terrestrial being

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone claims legal title over a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a creature from another world.

clue.text: Simon a bit perturbed? It's those high hopes

indicators.note: perturbed means disturbed, so the letters of Simon a bit are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Simon is a little upset about his lofty aspirations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitions are strong desires to achieve, aims set high.
